items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: Eddie Durham's brothers played in the band, one on bass and one on trombone.

ctx.x: Well when my brother and I got there we played about days and the contract was over. The job ended. And I said what is this? So the guy say, Eugene Coy, he says well don't worry about it. He says we're going to Amarillo, Texas. That's my home town, and we'll get further work there. And says my mother and father's there, and everything. He says so don't worry about a thing.

All right, so he had this one car, and incidentally, Eddie Durham's brothers played in the band, one on bass and one on trombone. And I'm very embarassed at this point that I can't remember their first names. I think -- I think one's name was Clyde, and I don't remember the other's name. Good musicians, like Eddy. And so we went in to Amarillo, Texas, and on the way, driving from Shawnee, Oklahoma to Amarillo, Texas we must have had about 13 or 14 blowouts, because all of this weight in this one car, with all of…

the wintertime.
So when we arrived in Amarillo, Texas it was 15 below zero! Can you imagine that? Up in the Panhandle. 15 below zero! And so when we got there Eugene Coy was really in his hometown, so he took as many people as he could to his parent's home, and the rest of us he put us up in a little hotel over a drugstore there. It was like what you may call like a shopping center, was about like a square block. They had a theater, and a hotel, a laundry, and whatnot.
